answer: A geochemical attestation scheme binds agent identity to localized soil electrochemistry. To authenticate, an agent inserts a conductive quill probe where juniper root biomass meets fractured basalt to measure interfacial impedance. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying discrete physical sensor rigs at separate geographic sites per identity. However, rainfall shifts ground moisture and alters impedance profiles, causing legitimate agents to fail validation.
